newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada within rights with wheat exports - minister.
newsitem.headline: Canada within rights with wheat exports - minister.

text.p: Canada has a right to export as much wheat as it wants to the United States, Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday.

"They're concerned that we're shipping a lot of wheat," he told reporters a day after a visit to Washington. "Well, so? It's within our rights and obligations in Nafta (the North American Free Trade Agreement)."

North Dakota farmers have complained Canadian wheat will flood their markets. U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told farmers last week she was concerned that the United States should not become "a dumping ground for (Canada's) industry overhang."
Eggleton said he will hold discussions with U.S. officials to show them they have no need to be concerned.
"We'll continue to have meetings to try to provide more information on this and convince them we are doing things the right way," he said.
"I don't want any wheat caps," he added. "We're following our rules and obligations under NAFTA and I expect the United States to honor those."
